summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness and fever. He was diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis due to a catheter-related E. coli infection, confirmed by urine culture. He was initially treated with vancomycin and cefepime, transitioned to Unasyn temporarily due to sensitivity concerns, then resumed cefepime when testing confirmed susceptibility. A PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV antibiotics at home. Imaging revealed bladder calculi, which were discussed with urology for planned outpatient removal to reduce recurrent infection risk. The patient had fecal incontinence with stool soiling of the catheter site and was managed with home health services for weekly catheter changes. He remained clinically stable, with resolution of fever and infection, and was discharged home on IV cefepime, methenamine, and vitamin C for UTI prophylaxis, with follow-up arranged.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Acute pyelonephritis without lesion of renal medullary necrosis
Other and unspecified Escherichia coli [E. coli]
